title: Personalized Multimodal Feedback Using Multiple External Representations: Strategy Profiles and Learning in High School Physics
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether students’ use of elaborated feedback in a digital high-school physics platform is associated with learning gains, and whether different patterns of feedback-format selection relate to performance. The authors are motivated by the growing relevance of adaptive feedback and multimodal large language models, but the study itself evaluates a computer-based learning environment rather than a generative AI coaching system for teachers.

The intervention-like component is a web platform (KI4SCool) that gave students verification feedback after multiple-choice physics exercises and optional elaborated feedback in three external representations: verbal, graphical/pictorial, and mathematical. Students could choose one, two, or all three formats after each item. The study analyzed naturally occurring usage patterns, linear mixed-effects models, and clustering of feedback-selection logs rather than assigning learners to conditions experimentally.

Participants were high-school students in grades 10 and 11 in Germany. Data came from 29 schools across four federal states, with 661 students who completed pre- and post-tests and at least one exercise included in the main analyses. The main findings were that greater use of elaborated feedback was modestly and positively associated with post-test performance, but the study was observational so causal claims are not warranted. The authors also found stable strategy groups in how students selected the three feedback formats, yet no strong evidence that these strategy groups were explained by initial representational competence. Overall, the paper suggests that multimodal, adaptive feedback may support physics learning, especially when students engage with multiple representations, but it does not study K–12 teacher coaching or lesson-plan feedback.

identified_tools.name: Adaptive Feedback System (General)
identified_tools.description: A computer-based instructional system that provides immediate verification feedback and optional elaborated feedback in multiple representational formats.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in high school physics to deliver verification feedback plus optional elaborated feedback (textual, graphical/pictorial, and mathematical) after multiple-choice exercises; the study examined how students selected and used these feedback formats and how that related to post-test learning.

findings.finding_summary: In two observational cohorts of high school physics students, more frequent use of elaborated feedback was associated with higher post-test scores. The association was statistically significant in Cohort 1 (standardized b2 = 0.13, 95% CI [0.05, 0.22]) and positive but not conventionally significant in Cohort 2 (b2 = 0.08, 95% CI [0.00, 0.16], p = .054); sample sizes were n = 351 and n = 310, respectively.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an observational cohort study with no randomized comparison of the feedback system, so causal claims are limited. The paper does provide quantitative modeling and cluster analyses, but the design remains correlational.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported association between elaborated feedback use and post-test performance is small but positive (standardized b2 around 0.080.13). That places the impact in the modest range rather than a large-effect tier.
